# Harness index

Every canonical skill, Claude command, and top-level repository tool route. The skill table
also records which of the three products can see each skill. One editable source (`.agents\skills\`)
reaches all three products; this file is how you check that it really did.

Connected MCP servers are listed in the generated capability router under `probe.mcp_servers`; read that roster for this device and list a server's tools before choosing `make-mcp`.
Project an explicit vault mirror with `Build-HarnessIndex.ps1 -ProjectVaultMirror`; verify both surfaces with `Build-HarnessIndex.ps1 -ProjectVaultMirror -Verify`.

Counts: **117 canonical skills**, **427 repository tool routes**, and **no Claude command files** -- `<repo>\commands\` holds only its `RETIRED.md`. Everything a command used to do is a canonical skill now, which is what makes it reachable from Codex and Cursor as well.

## Device and skill model

The repository remote `pyrgos-ai/doug-harness` is the source. A receiving computer follows `../ONBOARDING/START-HERE.md`; its bootstrap is idempotent and preserves product-owned settings, credentials, plugins, sessions, and user text outside managed markers.

| Surface | How canonical skills arrive |
|---|---|
| Claude and Cursor | Thin projections from `.agents/skills/` |
| Codex | Reads `~/.agents/skills/` directly; harness writes no Codex wrappers |
| Product-owned skills | Installed by the relevant product, never copied by this harness |

`surfaces:` controls **Claude/Cursor wrapper projection only** — it never hides a canonical package from Codex, which reads the canonical root directly. A product-specific skill must state that constraint in its own `SKILL.md`.

`INDEX.md` is the generated catalogue of canonical skills and command history. Its Codex visibility and budget figures are a source-device snapshot; use it to discover owners, then inspect the installed skill root and current product configuration on the receiving machine. Regenerate from a harness clone when verifying a changed canonical tree.

- **There is no separate Claude global-config repository.** Douglas retired that architecture on 2026-08-10. The archived `douglaspmcgowan/claude-config` repository is historical; the former global-config GitHub name resolves to `pyrgos-ai/doug-harness`, so treating it as a second authority risks cloning the harness over `~\.claude`. Cross-agent material is canonical under this repository's `.agents\` tree and reaches Claude through managed projections; Claude settings, hook wiring, sessions, permissions, and authentication remain machine-local under `~\.claude` and are never mirrored back into Git. `Manage-Harness.ps1 -Action InstallGlobal` reconciles harness and projections; it expects no Git remote under `~\.claude`.


## Review surfaces

`skills\review\SKILL.md` is the router and the single-reviewer — "review this" names no surface, so it reads the target's scope and failure category and picks between a single-perspective pass, an independent-perspective panel, a defect-class lens sweep, and a pre-merge worktree review. Pointed at this harness's own hooks, loops, rules, and safety edges it runs its own harness mode; Hook reviews exercise synthetic stdin payloads and expected verdicts in a real subprocess rather than reasoning about what the hook would do.


## Data, secrets, and vaults

- Git carries source, contracts, safe fixtures, task state, and documentation. Project manifests declare external data, placement, authority, adapters, integrity checks, and recovery.
- `data-manifest.yaml` and `Invoke-DeclaredProjectData.ps1` own project-data restore and publication. SQLite snapshots, DVC artifacts, Drive, and network services remain project-declared authorities.
- `secret-manifest.json` is value-free. `Invoke-WithBitwardenSecret.ps1` is the one-secret-to-one-process broker; it never grants unattended secret use without a separately approved allowlist grant. `Invoke-WithEnvSecret.ps1 -CommandId <id>` is its sibling for secrets already in the User or Machine Windows environment (for example `CANVAS_PAT`): it injects the variables pinned in `env-command-allowlist.json` into that one fixed child and redacts them from output; `adapters/claude/settings-rules.json` allowlists it for auto mode.
- `Find-PromptCorpus.ps1` (``& 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .agents/tools/Find-PromptCorpus.ps1 -CorpusRoot <path> -AllowedRoot <path>``) performs local, user-only JSONL retrieval only within caller-supplied allowed roots; rejects reparse and protected-suffix inputs, suppresses secret-like results, creates no corpus copy, cache, index, embedding, network call, hook, or telemetry.
- `Invoke-GmailReadOnlyQuery.ps1` accepts an account selector and arbitrary query in a POST JSON body, permits only `gmail.readonly`, and reports live execution `could-not-tell` when its credential broker is unavailable.
- `Read-LocalAppRoster.ps1` reports `pass` with the measured population, or `could-not-tell` with a null population when the device roster is absent, unreadable, or empty.
- The vault holds authored knowledge and links; project runtime data never lives there — the repository owns source and safe configuration, the declared data root owns external and runtime data, and a vault note links to that owner rather than carrying a copy. Read `VAULT-PROTOCOL.md` before a vault call, then the active vault's `IA.md`; prohibited paths stay excluded from reads, searches, mirrors, and logs.
- `Sync-VaultMirror.ps1`, `Invoke-VaultLint.ps1`, and their tests are the current deterministic vault utilities. Google Drive Desktop already synchronizes its own local folder — never add a second copy job over a selected folder inside it. The `sync-obsidian` workflow was that duplicate; archived under `archive\skills-retired-20260823\`, and neither it nor an improvised replacement is a second sync system.
- `Sync-VaultMirror.ps1` treats destination `.github\` as repository-owned automation and excludes it from robocopy `/MIR`, alongside the existing root-file exclusions. The regression fixture commits `.github\workflows\fixture.yml`, runs the real tool under `-DryRun`, and asserts the workflow survives; removing the exclusion fails only that case while the other nine remain green.
- Obsidian runtime and Sync facts, including the diagnostic lesson that expected-file absence cannot establish state, live in `VAULT-REFERENCE.md` → **Obsidian runtime and Sync**; use that section before diagnosing a vault.

`Find-PromptCorpus.ps1` (``& 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .agents/tools/Find-PromptCorpus.ps1 -CorpusRoot <path> -AllowedRoot <path>``) is retrieval; three skills own the questions asked of what it returns. `skills\detective\SKILL.md` finds patterns and automation candidates across recent sessions, transcripts, work records, or structured project history. `skills\investigate\SKILL.md` establishes root cause and full impact of one specific incident. `skills\trainer\SKILL.md` reads one canonical skill's real usage history for improvement opportunities; both it and detective stop rather than invent when data is too thin to carry a claim.


## Cloud and receiving devices

`../ONBOARDING/START-HERE.md` is the receiving-device checklist: installed prerequisites, value-free MCP templates, GitHub authentication, and the explicit OAuth/credential boundary. `software.json` and `Test-ExecutableDiscovery.ps1` (``& 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .agents/tools/Test-ExecutableDiscovery.ps1 -UserPathOverride <path>``) own machine command discovery.

For hosted work, each project owns `.agents/cloud/setup.sh`, `maintenance.sh`, and `verify.sh`; `../ONBOARDING/CLOUD-AGENTS.md` owns provider setup and authorization. `.agents/cloud/credential-profile.sh` decides whether an unset Bitwarden or Docket variable is a failure or an absence to move past: none of the four set skips (not a code-work environment), a partial set fails (half-provisioned kit), and `CLOUD_KIT_PROFILE=full` requires all four — without it an uncredentialed cloud agent could never reach a green verifier. A cloud agent uses repository instructions and committed/project-bound skills first. If the global harness is absent, verify access to the private harness repository before relying on an unbound global skill or design leaf. When an agent needs portable repository material, `skills\package\SKILL.md` owns the clean-clone-verified package.
`CLOUD-PROTOCOL.md` resolves and read-only verifies the environment id for a published GitHub repository; creation and GitHub app authorization remain human browser steps.


## Quarantine and retired material

- Retired Claude commands are archived under `archive/commands-retired-20260827/`; current cross-product capabilities live in `.agents/skills/`. The live retirement registry is the generated block below, not a hand-written ledger.
- Root `skills/` is quarantined staging material, not an installed skill root; do not project it. Ruled 2026-08-30: everything outside the canonical three (`slides`, `html-slides`, `frontend-slides` under `.agents/skills/`) was archived to `archive/skills-retired-20260830/quarantine-slides/`, licences included. What remains here — `chrome-cdp`, `client`, `feedback`, `rollover-session` — is not slide material and was not covered by that ruling.
- `archive/` is frozen forensic retention, not active runtime code.

## Repository tools

Every tracked, stable, first-party executable at the top level of `.agents\tools`. The shared
repository file-set owner defines the candidate shape; capability routes and classifications
must resolve inside it. PowerShell routes carry a safe `Get-Help` discovery command through
`Show-ToolHelp.ps1`, which runs nothing and is reachable under the host PowerShell guard; other
runtimes carry their exact path because they have no shared, side-effect-free help switch.

## Retired paths and names

`manifests/retired-paths.json` is authoritative: **232 retired paths** and **66 retired names**. Retiring something means adding its entry in the same commit; `Test-HarnessPathClaims.ps1` and `Test-RetiredNames.ps1` (``& 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .agents/tools/Test-RetiredNames.ps1 -RepoRoot <path>``) enforce it.

## Interface design route

Any task that produces or changes an interface follows this route before implementation:
`~/.agents/DESIGN.md` → `~/.agents/design/dashboards.md` for dashboard-shaped work.
The dashboard route also reads the mission-control representation and aesthetic studies, and records the chosen representation's nine → ninety answer.

For concrete design material, use the existing library router:

| Start at | For |
|---|---|
| `~/.agents/design/LIBRARIES.md` | The router. A pointer table to every leaf -- read it there rather than from any copied list, including this one. |
| `~/.agents/DESIGN.md` | The universal interface rules, and the precedence order when they and `impeccable` disagree. |
| `~/.agents/design/dashboards.md` | Rules for operational, analytical, and reporting data surfaces. |
| `~/.agents/design/mission-control/REPRESENTATIONS.md` | Representation choice and nine → ninety scaling. |
| `~/.agents/design/mission-control/AESTHETIC-OPTIONS.md` | Visual directions for operational surfaces. |
| `~/.agents/design/mission-control/REPRESENTATIONS.md` | Rules and representation choices for dashboards and operational data surfaces; pair with `AESTHETIC-OPTIONS.md` for visual direction. |
| `~/.agents/design/languages/registry.md` | Whether a committed visual world already exists, checked before inventing another. |

`impeccable` is the process that consumes the rules and library. Its visual completion bar lives in `verification-before-completion`.

## How each product loads skills and commands

Verified 2026-08-06 against local configuration and current official documentation.
Every claim below names the file inspected or the doc it came from.

| | Claude Code | Codex CLI | Cursor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Version checked | 2.1.128 | codex-cli 0.123.0 | desktop app |
| Reads `~\.agents\skills` directly | no | **yes** | **yes** |
| Needs a projected wrapper | yes, `~\.claude\skills\` | no | `~\.cursor\skills\` (legacy; now redundant) |
| Other skill roots | `.claude/skills/`, plugins, enterprise | repo `.agents/skills`, `/etc/codex/skills`, bundled, plugins | `.agents/skills`, `.cursor/skills`, plus `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.codex/skills` for compatibility |
| Separate commands system | **merged into skills** | custom prompts, **deprecated** | none separate |
| Slash invocation of a skill | `/skill-name` | `/skill-name` | `/` menu in Agent chat |
| Listing budget | **1% of context window**, tunable | **2% of context window** (8,000 chars if unknown), not tunable | not documented |
| Behavior when over budget | **drops descriptions**, never the name; least-used first | **omits whole skills**, alphabetical tail first | not documented |
| Per-entry cap | 1,536 chars (`description` + `when_to_use`) | none documented | none documented |

### What this actually means

**Claude Code never hides a skill.** The listing always contains every skill *name*;
when it overflows, Claude Code strips *descriptions*, starting with the skills you
invoke least. A skill can therefore go quiet (Claude stops auto-triggering it because
the keywords are gone) while `/name` still works perfectly. Raise the budget with the
`skillListingBudgetFraction` setting or the `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET
environment variable; demote individual entries to `"name-only"` via `skillOverrides`.
Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills>.

**Claude Code merged commands into skills.** `.claude/commands/deploy.md` and
`.claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md` both produce `/deploy`, and **the skill wins on a name
conflict**. A canonical skill therefore already carries its own `/name` ergonomics --
no thin command wrapper is needed, and a same-named command file is inert.
Source: <https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills>.

**Past its budget, Codex cuts every description at once.** The budget is a *character*
budget, not a skill count. Measured on codex-cli 0.155.0 (2026-09-28), an over-long list
gets one shared description cap, lowered until the list fits: every skill loses the tail
of its routing text together, and only when descriptions are empty do entries drop off
the end. codex-cli 0.123.0 (2026-08-06) instead evicted the alphabetical tail whole. Either
way, the only lever we control is description length at the source.
Sources: <https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills>, and `codex debug prompt-input`.

**Codex custom prompts (`~/.codex/prompts/*.md`, invoked `/prompts:name`) are
deprecated**, and OpenAI now points at skills for reusable instructions. There is no
Codex commands system worth targeting -- which is why commands converge on skills here.
Source: <https://developers.openai.com/codex/custom-prompts>.

**Cursor reads `~/.agents/skills` natively** and also reads `~/.claude/skills` for
compatibility, so the `~/.cursor/skills` wrapper this harness installs is redundant.
It is *not*, however, the cause of double-listing. Measured 2026-08-06: all 58
projected skills exist identically in all three roots, so root redundancy would
double **every** skill -- yet Douglas saw `brainstorming` doubled while `conductor`
and `task` were single. The real cause is Cursor's own skill cache in
`%APPDATA%\Cursor\User\globalStorage\state.vscdb`, which still lists all 20
`source-command-*` wrapper skills retired from disk on 2026-08-06, pointing at
`~\.claude\skills\source-command-*` paths that no longer exist. The four-way match is
exact: `brainstorming` and `task` had wrappers (stale sibling shows); `conductor` and
`boss-update` never did (no sibling). That cache is product-owned -- the harness must
not edit it, and it clears when Cursor restarts and re-indexes. The redundant
`~/.cursor/skills` root therefore stays: removing it was never the fix, and no
evidence yet shows it costs anything. Source: <https://cursor.com/docs/skills.md>.

### Codex budget math

- Measured list budget: **21,502 characters** (`codex debug prompt-input`, 2026-09-28, codex-cli 0.155.0, gpt-6-astra).
- Codex system + plugin skills consume **2,623**, leaving **18,879** for canonical skills.
- The 117 canonical skills currently cost **15,887 characters**.
- 1 skill(s) set `disable-model-invocation: true` and cost nothing: `correct`. They stay invokable as `/name` on Claude and Codex but never appear in the model-visible listing -- by design, not by cap.
- **Under budget with 2,992 characters of headroom. All 117 canonical skills are visible to Codex.**

### Claude budget math

The formula is `contextWindow x bytesPerToken x skillListingBudgetFraction`, with
`bytesPerToken` fixed at 4 and the fraction defaulting to `0.01` -- the 8,000-character
default everyone reports. It is not on the official skills page; it is stated in
<https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/64606>. `SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET`
overrides the whole computation with a fixed count when set.

- This device: 200,000 tokens x 4 x 0.06 = **48,000 characters**. The fraction is per-device and product-owned; `InstallGlobal` does not reproduce it, so a different machine needs it set by hand and this arithmetic re-checked.
- Claude reads `description` **and** `when_to_use`, so an entry here weighs far more than the same entry on Codex. The 117 canonical skills cost **12,774 characters** -- 0.8x their Codex weight.
- **There are no command files left to share the budget with.** `<repo>\commands\` holds only
  its `RETIRED.md`, so the shared-budget question that used to change this arithmetic by the
  whole answer -- one formatter over one list, or two -- is moot on this tree. It returns the
  moment a command file does, including one written by hand into `~\.claude\commands\`, which
  no generator here reproduces or sees.
- **Headroom: 12,774 used of 48,000, leaving 35,226 characters** -- about **320 more model-visible skills** at the current 110-character mean entry. A user-only skill costs nothing and is not on this count at all, which is why 1 of the 117 canonical skills are absent from it.

## Canonical skills

Source of truth: `.agents\skills\<name>\SKILL.md`. Projected by
`Manage-Harness.ps1 -Action InstallGlobal`.

A skill may declare an optional `surfaces:` list to narrow which product projections
it receives; omitting the key means every surface. Codex is never narrowed by it,
because it only ever reads canonical.

There is no Cursor column, and its absence is the answer rather than a gap: Cursor
reads `~\.agents\skills` natively (see the table above), so dropping `cursor` from
`surfaces:` costs the `~\.cursor\skills` wrapper and never the skill. The column
therefore read `yes` for every skill in the tree, and its other value would not have
changed what anyone did. The Claude and Codex columns are kept separate even where
they agree: one is computed from `surfaces:` and the other from the character cap.

## Claude commands

**There are none, and that is the finished state rather than a gap.** A command file was
read by Claude Code and by nothing else -- Codex reads `~\.agents\skills` natively and Cursor
reads both skill roots, and neither has ever read `~\.claude\commands\`. So a capability that
lived in `commands\` existed on one product out of three. `Promote-CommandsToSkills.ps1` (``& 'C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe' -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File .agents/tools/Promote-CommandsToSkills.ps1 -RepoRoot <path> -Verify``) moved
all of them across and the files themselves are gone; `<repo>\commands\RETIRED.md` is what
remains. Every promoted skill is user-only, so it stays invokable as `/name` on all three
products and spends no listing budget. `Promote-CommandsToSkills.ps1 -Verify` is the gate that
keeps the gap from reopening: it fails if a command file exists with no canonical skill.

index and to the budget arithmetic above.
